description: Metric definitions (Module 1). Each metric is written once and computed by common.metric(). {where} is replaced by the period filter on event_date.

active_users.definition: Distinct users with at least one clean event (any type) in the period.
active_users.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events_clean WHERE {where}

buyers.definition: Distinct users with at least one order in the period.
buyers.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM orders WHERE {where}

orders.definition: Number of orders (user + session + timestamp groups of purchase lines).

order_lines.definition: Number of purchased product lines (clean purchase events).
order_lines.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events_clean WHERE event_type = 'purchase' AND {where}

revenue.definition: Gross revenue: sum of unit price over purchased lines (the log has no quantity; one line = one unit, an assumption).
revenue.sql: SELECT SUM(price) FROM events_clean WHERE event_type = 'purchase' AND {where}

net_revenue.definition: Revenue minus refund candidates (negative-price purchase rows, assumed to be refunds).
net_revenue.sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(price) FROM events_clean WHERE event_type = 'purchase' AND {where}) + (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(price), 0) FROM refund_candidates WHERE {where})

aov.sql: SELECT SUM(revenue) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE {where}

payer_rate.definition: Buyers / active users in the same period.
payer_rate.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM orders WHERE {where}) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events_clean WHERE {where})

cart_adds.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events_clean WHERE event_type = 'cart' AND {where}

cart_removals.definition: Clean 'Product Removed from Cart' events. Unreliable: 11.41% of (user, product) pairs remove a product not in the cart at some point, even after cleaning (Module 1); use for monitoring only, not conclusions.
cart_removals.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events_clean WHERE event_type = 'remove_from_cart' AND {where}

new_users.definition: Users whose first clean event in the data falls in the period. Not meaningful for October 2019: the data starts then, so everyone looks new (Module 2).
new_users.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT user_id, MIN(event_date) AS event_date FROM events_clean GROUP BY user_id) WHERE {where}
